title: A piston moves inward
hook: Change one condition and watch the gas respond.

knows: A gas has pressure, volume, temperature and an amount.
doesNotKnow: At fixed temperature and gas amount, PV is constant. Halving volume from 2 L to 1 L doubles pressure from 1 atm to 2 atm.

misconception: Changing one gas variable always leaves the others unchanged.
objective: Use the ideal gas law with the stated fixed conditions.

claims.text: Question, chart and reveal: An ideal gas starts at 1 atm and 2 L. At constant temperature and amount, the piston compresses it to 1 L. What is its final pressure? At fixed temperature and gas amount, PV is constant. Halving volume from 2 L to 1 L doubles pressure from 1 atm to 2 atm.
claims.source: PV = nRT under the stated fixed conditions; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/9-summary

claims.text: Dots are schematic and not individual real gas molecules; the piston is an idealized representation and the model does not predict deviations from ideal behavior.
Recall: In an ideal gas with temperature and amount fixed, what happens to pressure when volume is halved? At fixed temperature and amount, PV is constant.

recall.question: In an ideal gas with temperature and amount fixed, what happens to pressure when volume is halved?
recall.why: At fixed temperature and amount, PV is constant.
